topic: Requirements to executable specifications and code generation

findings.message: slide 6 ('Structuring Requirements with Pytest Specifications'): [clarity] The example test code calls `calculate_discount` which is not defined or imported, making the specification non-executable as written; students may think it can run immediately. Fix: Add a comment indicating the function is imported from the module under test, or show a stub import.

slide 8 ('Step 1: Writing Executable Specs for a Module Contract'): [clarity] The `pytest.raises` `match` parameter uses a plain string which is interpreted as a regex pattern; students might assume it requires an exact match. Fix: Note that `match` is a regex pattern, or use a raw string `match=r"Insufficient funds"` to make the regex nature explicit.

evidence.title: Step 1: Writing Executable Specs for a Module Contract

findings.message: slide 9 ('Step 2: Generating and Verifying Implementation Against Specs'): [clarity] The AI-generated implementation adds a `deposit` method not present in the original interface stub or test suite, which may imply the AI can extend the public interface beyond the spec. Fix: Either include `deposit` in the executable specification or add a note that the AI introduced an extra method not required by the given spec.

evidence.title: Step 2: Generating and Verifying Implementation Against Specs

findings.message: slide 12 ('Automated Feedback Loops for Code Refinement'): [clarity] The flow diagram step "Pass or Feedback Loop" is ambiguous; it conflates two distinct outcomes. Fix: Split into two branches: "Pass" and "Feedback Loop" to clearly show the iterative cycle.

evidence.title: Automated Feedback Loops for Code Refinement
